items.title: Mortgage and Loan Insurance Programs Under the National Housing Act-Debenture Interest Rates
items.summary: This notice announces changes in the interest rates to be paid on debentures issued with respect to a loan or mortgage insured by the Federal Housing Administration under the provisions of the National Housing Act (the Act). The interest rate for debentures issued under Section 221(g)(4) of the Act during the 6-month period beginning January 1, 2026, is 4 percent. The interest rate for debentures issued under any other provision of the Act is the rate in effect on the date that the commitment to insure the loan or mortgage was issued, or the date that the loan or mortgage was endorsed (or initially endorsed if there are two or more endorsements) for insurance, whichever rate is higher. The interest rate for debentures issued under these other provisions with respect to a loan or mortgage committed or endorsed during the 6-month period beginning January 1, 2026, is 4\3/4\ percent.

trends_raw:
- **Volume and novelty:** 170 evidence candidates, none of them first surfaced in this run. This is a consolidation cycle, not a breaking one; the value is in depth and assembly rather than speed.
- **Baseline:** No previous run sits in the archive, so there is nothing to compare against yet. Treat this run's topic mix as the starting reference point.
- **Shape of the run:** Medicare and Medicaid dominate with 30 items drawn from nine sources, followed by long-term care (19), housing (13), workforce (12), financial security (10) and palliative and hospice care (9). Government data is doing most of the work, with the CMS provider data catalog and the BLS API behind the largest share of high-scoring items.
- **Coverage posture:** 82 items are confirmed gaps against monitored publishers and 78 fall on beats where no monitored publisher is being watched, out of 65 monitored publishers in a 132-publisher registry. The unwatched share should be read as blind spot in our monitoring, not as an absence of competitors.
- **Where competitors are actually present:** Financial security is the most contested cluster, with 4 of 10 items already matched. Medicare and Medicaid shows 3 matches in 30 items, long-term care 2 in 19, workforce 2 in 12. Housing (0 of 13) and palliative and hospice care (0 of 9) are entirely unmatched.
- **Recency:** Long-term care carries an item published today, and Medicare/Medicaid, workforce, caregiving and mental health items are all three days old or newer, so the freshness argument holds for at least another news cycle.
- **Watch item:** A RAND report on space defense industrial base workforce shortfalls surfaced in the workforce cluster. It is off-beat and should be filtered out before it distorts the workforce count in the next run.
feature_pitch_raw:
- **The story:** Every federal file that describes a nursing home, hospice, clinician or equipment supplier was refreshed inside a single month, and the labor and price data needed to explain what those files show landed at the same time. Nine independent sources fed the Medicare/Medicaid cluster this run across 30 items, 27 of which no monitored publisher has matched.
- **The spine:** CMS refreshed Health Deficiencies, Fire Safety Deficiencies, Penalties, Ownership, Provider Information, Survey Summary, Inspection Dates, MDS Quality Measures and the Nursing Home Data Collection Intervals table (which carries the staffing measure periods) all on August 1, plus Skilled Nursing Facility Quality Reporting Program data the same day, national and state CAHPS Hospice Survey files on August 7, and Medical Equipment Suppliers on August 30.
- **The second layer:** BLS puts nursing care facilities employment at 1,592.90 thousand jobs in July 2026 (+2.6% year over year), continuing care retirement communities and assisted living at 1,028.20 thousand (+1.5%), and home health care services at 1,886.10 thousand (+4.8%). Medical care CPI stands at 593.78 (1982-84=100), up 1.7%, while home health average hourly earnings of $27.91 rose only 1.2% and assisted living and CCRC earnings of $25.47 rose 3.2%.
- **The policy frame:** A Justice in Aging primer on Medicaid home and community-based services (August 20), three KFF data notes dated August 26, and a Center for Retirement Research analysis of a proposal to shift Medicare funding to states supply the argument over who pays for what the data describes.
- **Why now:** The newest item in the cluster is three days old, and 27 of 30 items carry a confirmed coverage gap.
- **Build it out:** Six items in the cluster break below the national level and 10 sit on structured public data, so state, metro and facility-level versions plus rankings, maps and trend lines come straight from the files rather than from interviews.
pitch_ideas_raw:
- **The full nursing home file, rebuilt in one sitting (CMS provider data, refreshed August 1):** Ownership, Penalties, Health Deficiencies, Fire Safety Deficiencies, Survey Summary, Inspection Dates, Provider Information and MDS Quality Measures were all refreshed together, each carrying three years of citations or scores at state and county level. Hook: join ownership to penalties and citation severity and rank operators, not just buildings. All eight are confirmed gaps against monitored publishers, and the long-term care cluster shows 17 gaps in 19 items.
- **Hospice quality, national and state, with nobody in the room (CMS, August 7):** The National and State CAHPS Hospice Survey files landed the same day. Hook: state-by-state family experience scores for Medicare-certified hospices, mapped. The palliative and hospice cluster is nine items with nine confirmed gaps and zero monitored coverage, the cleanest open beat in the run.
- **Who supplies the equipment (CMS Medical Equipment Suppliers, August 30, score 74):** A location-level list of what each supplier carries and whether it participates in Medicare. Hook: county-level supply deserts for wheelchairs, oxygen and other durable equipment, a consumer service story and a payer story at once. Confirmed gap.
- **Caregiver pay is losing to medical inflation (BLS, June and July 2026):** Home health average hourly earnings of $27.91 grew 1.2% year over year against a 1.7% rise in the medical care CPI, while assisted living and CCRC pay of $25.47 grew 3.2%. Hook: the fastest-growing setting by headcount, home health at +4.8%, is also the one where wages moved least. Ten of 12 workforce items are confirmed gaps.
- **Older workers as a labor supply story (BLS, July 2026):** Employment among people 65 and over reached 11,538 thousand, up 1.4%. Hook: pair with the senior living staffing series and ask trade readers whether their own residents and prospects are part of the workforce they are short of.
- **HUD sets the rent ceiling for FY 2027 (Federal Register, September 1, 2026):** The Fair Market Rents notice explains the calculation method and the reevaluation process public housing agencies must follow under the Housing Opportunity Through Modernization Act of 2016. Hook: what the new numbers mean for voucher holders aging in place and for the operators who accept them. All 13 housing items in this run are confirmed gaps, with zero monitored coverage.
- **Disparate impact, round two (HUD supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking, August 10):** HUD is continuing an effort begun with a January 2026 proposal to remove its disparate-impact regulations and leave the question to the courts, and is also amending its Title VI regulations. Hook: what removal would mean for age-adjacent fair housing complaints in senior housing. Confirmed gap.
- **Two Social Security actions in one week (Federal Register):** SSR 26-2p, published September 1, consolidates policy on documenting and evaluating disability in young adults and rescinds SSR 11-2p; a separate August 31 notice rescinds Acquiescence Ruling 90-2(2) on treating a rental subsidy as in-kind income for SSI benefit calculations. Hook: the rental subsidy rescission is a household budget story for SSI recipients living with family. The SSR is a confirmed gap; the rescission shows light monitored coverage, so move quickly or go deeper.
- **HCBS, explained before the next budget fight (Justice in Aging, August 20):** A primer on how Medicaid home and community-based services support older adults with disabilities and the policy gaps limiting access. Hook: pair it with the Center for Retirement Research analysis of shifting Medicare costs to states for a single piece on how much of the long-term care system rests on state decisions. Confirmed gap.
- **The KFF August 26 trio:** Medicaid coverage for women, the Medicaid/CHIP monthly enrollment tracker, and an analysis of rural hospitals providing inpatient maternity care to Medicaid enrollees. Hook for our audience: the rural hospital piece is a rural aging story in disguise, since the same facilities anchor emergency and post-acute care for older residents. All three are confirmed gaps.
- **Telehealth and the palliative conversation (RAND, August 31):** A qualitative study of patient and family caregiver experiences with telehealth versus in-person outpatient palliative care visits, including preferences by mode and perceived differences in communication quality after the pandemic. Hook: a consumer piece on what families should ask for when a serious-illness conversation is scheduled by video. Confirmed gap.
- **Two quiet Medicare notices worth a trade brief (Federal Register):** The RAPID coverage pathway notice with comment period (August 11) sets out how CMS will grant expedited national coverage to eligible new devices, and an August 13 advisory tells Qualifying APM Participants how to update billing information so incentive payments can be disbursed. Hook: the second is money sitting undelivered; the first is the route new devices take into Medicare. Both confirmed gaps.
- **The state aging profile as an evergreen anchor (American Community Survey, 2023 five-year estimates):** State counts for the 65+, 65-74, 75-84 and 85+ populations with median household income and housing tenure across 52 geographies, including 5,994,486 residents 65 and older in California and 4,630,733 in Florida. Hook: the denominator table for every localized version of the CMS facility stories above. Confirmed gap.
